   293	\paragraph{Direct index sampling (candidate direction, recommended).}
   294	Define, for arbitrary $m' \ge 1$, the line-point distribution over
   295	$\F_q^{m'}$ that samples the uniform point, the uniform axis index
   296	$i \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$, and the diagonal direction with vanishing first
   297	$i-1$ coordinates, directly; define the \emph{directly indexed game} with
   298	this question distribution, whose line questions carry the index $i$ (and,
   299	for diagonal lines, the projected direction) in place of the seed
   300	$s \in \F_q$; and state the imported soundness theorem for that game
   301	(form~4 above).  This removes the divisibility obstruction and nothing
   302	else: the directly indexed game still asks for polynomials on revealed
   303	lines, has no pair questions, and weighs its branches as the present game
   304	does, so establishing form~4 carries the same two import obligations as
   305	the $\chi$-based import (Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations}), now at
   306	arbitrary dimension.
   307	
   308	The relation to the present game when $m' \mid q$ must moreover be proved
   309	at the level of games, not merely of question distributions, because the
   310	two games have different question alphabets: an $\mathsf{ALine}$ question
   311	of the $\chi$-based game is a pair $(u_0, s)$ and a $\mathsf{DLine}$
   312	question a triple $(u_0, s, v')$, so a strategy may select different
   313	measurements for seeds $s \ne s'$ with $\chi(s) = \chi(s')$, and equality
   314	of the induced laws of the geometric data does not by itself transport
   315	such a strategy.  The transport layer decomposes into the following
   316	obligations, none of which is carried out here.
   317	\begin{itemize}
   318	  \item \emph{Distribution lemma.}  When $m' \mid q$, the image of the
   319	  conditionally linear question distribution under the parsing map
   320	  $(u_0,s) \mapsto (u_0,\chi(s))$, $(u_0,s,v') \mapsto (u_0,\chi(s),v')$
   321	  is the direct distribution, and conditioned on the parsed question the
   322	  seed is uniform on the class $\chi^{-1}(i)$, independently of everything
   323	  else.
   324	  \item \emph{Parsing pullback.}  A strategy for the directly indexed game
   325	  composed with the parsing map is a seed-oblivious strategy for the
   326	  $\chi$-based game.  Since the win predicate depends on the question only
   327	  through the parsed data, and a seed-oblivious strategy answers
   328	  identically across each fiber --- in particular on the synchronicity
   329	  branches, where both players hold the same seed --- the value should be
   330	  preserved exactly on every branch, and projectivity is preserved.  This
   331	  is the direction the combining subtree needs.
   332	  \item \emph{Seed-fiber averaging: what it preserves and what it does
   333	  not.}  In the opposite direction, average each line measurement over its
   334	  seed fiber: attach to a direct question $(u_0,i)$, respectively
   335	  $(u_0,i,v')$, the average over uniform $s \in \chi^{-1}(i)$ of the
   336	  measurements attached to $(u_0,s)$, respectively $(u_0,s,v')$, leaving
   337	  the points measurements unchanged.  By the conditional uniformity of the
   338	  seed this preserves the value of every \emph{line-versus-point} branch
   339	  exactly: there the paired question carries no seed, so the branch value
   340	  is an average over the fiber of per-seed values, which the averaged
   341	  measurement computes.  It does \emph{not} preserve the synchronicity
   342	  branches.  There both players hold the same seed, so the $\chi$-based
   343	  branch value is the diagonal average
   344	  $\E_{s}\sum_f \langle M^{(u_0,s)}_f \ot \widetilde M^{(u_0,s)}_f
   345	  \rangle$, while the averaged strategy realizes the double average
   346	  $\E_{s,s'}\sum_f \langle M^{(u_0,s)}_f \ot \widetilde M^{(u_0,s')}_f
   347	  \rangle$ over independent seeds in the fiber; the two differ whenever
   348	  the players' measurements vary across a fiber in a correlated way (if
   349	  both apply a common seed-dependent relabelling, every diagonal term is
   350	  large and the cross terms are not), and neither quantity dominates the
   351	  other in general.  An earlier revision of this note claimed that the
   352	  averaging preserves the exact value, and with it synchronicity; that
   353	  claim was wrong and is withdrawn.  What needs proof is control of the
   354	  synchronicity branches under de-seeding.  Candidate approaches: show
   355	  that a strategy of value $1-\eps$ in the $\chi$-based game is, with
   356	  polynomial loss, close to a seed-oblivious one; or state form~4 with a
   357	  synchronicity hypothesis in the doubled-average form and re-derive it on
   358	  the tensor-code side.  Choosing and proving one of these is an open
   359	  obligation.
   360	  \item \emph{Projectivity round trip.}  The averaged strategy is a POVM
   361	  strategy even when the given one is projective, while the imported
   362	  theorem, like the present one, takes projective strategies.  The
   363	  intended round trip is: dilate the averaged strategy to a projective one
   364	  (Naimark preserves all product correlations
   365	  $\langle X \ot Y \rangle$ of the given strategy against the dilated
   366	  state --- hence the value of every branch the averaging preserved ---
   367	  but nothing restores the diagonal seed correlations once the averaging
   368	  has been performed); apply form~4; and compress the resulting polynomial
   369	  measurement along the dilation isometry back to a POVM in the required
   370	  measurement class on the original space.  That this compression
   371	  preserves the consistency conclusions must itself be proved; it is
   372	  stated here as an obligation, not established.  (Alternatively, form~4
   373	  may be stated for POVM strategies outright, moving the dilation inside
   374	  the import.)
   375	\end{itemize}

   394	The external check that the tensor-code test of arXiv:2111.08131 samples
   395	its axes and subcubes directly has been made against that source: Figure~1
   396	there draws the axis index and the subcube data uniformly and directly,
   397	with no index encoding into $\F_q$.
   398	
   399	\paragraph{Padding the dimension.}
   400	Alternatively, embed the combined polynomial into
   401	$\mathrm{ideg}_{d,\bar m}(\F_q)$ for $\bar m = 4m$, the least power of two
   402	with $\bar m \ge 2m+2$, ignoring the $2m-2$ dummy variables.  Then
   403	$\bar m \mid q$ holds whenever $q \ge 4m$, and the existing game applies at
   404	dimension $\bar m$.  In the complementary regime $m \in \{q/2,\, q\}$ the
   405	conclusion is vacuous: $md \ge q/2$ gives
   406	$\delta_S \ge a(md)^a q^{-b} \ge a\,2^{-a} q^{a-b} \ge a\,2^{-b} \ge 1$
   407	for $a \ge 2$, while the consistency quantities bounded by the theorem never
   408	exceed $1$.  This route stays inside the present definitions but reworks the
   409	sub-line distribution (a fourth coordinate block of dummies), the combining
   410	map, and the wrong-block Schwartz--Zippel analysis, and it moves the
   411	combining lemmas away from their source statements at dimension $2m+2$.
   412	
   413	\paragraph{Unequal index classes.}
   414	One could instead define an index function at dimension $2m+2$ with classes
   415	of sizes $\lfloor q/(2m+2)\rfloor$ and $\lceil q/(2m+2)\rceil$.  The index
   416	is then only approximately uniform, the identification with the external
   417	test fails exactly, and every distributional identity in the sub-line
   418	analysis acquires an error term; this amounts to re-proving the imported
   419	soundness theorem for a perturbed game and is not recommended.
   420	
   421	\section{Comparison with the blueprint}
   422	
   423	The blueprint \cite{MIPStarREBlueprint} keeps the sub-line lemma, the
   424	combined line lemma, and the polynomial-pair lemma in their source-shaped
   425	statements, with no divisibility hypothesis.  Their proofs retain the source
   426	constructions and mark the unresolved obligation at the exact steps: the
   427	first sampling step of the sub-line construction, where $\chi_{2m+2}$ and
   428	the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$ are invoked, and the
   429	instantiation step of the polynomial-pair proof, where $(q,2m+2,d,1)$ is
   430	used as a game parameter tuple.  A chapter remark records the divisibility
   431	arithmetic and cites this note; the final soundness theorem for the Pauli
   432	basis test remains open modulo this obligation.  The blueprint's proof node
   433	for the classical soundness import itself states the source's route --- the
   434	identification with the two-prover tensor-code test and the application of
   435	Theorem~4.7 --- and enumerates the two obligations of
   436	Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations} as open, citing this note for the
   437	detailed comparison and the case arithmetic.  An earlier revision had
   438	instead added the hypothesis $2m+2 \mid q$ to the three lemmas; that was
   439	statement drift in the sense of the proof-gap protocol, since the hypothesis
   440	excludes all admissible $m \ge 2$ and does not appear in the source.
   441	
   442	\section{Conclusion}
   443	
   444	There is a theorem-level gap in the source proof route: the classical low
   445	individual degree game invoked at dimension $2m+2$ is undefined for every
   446	admissible tuple with $m \ge 2$ (and for $(q,m) = (2,1)$), because its
   447	question distribution requires $2m+2 \mid q$ while admissibility supplies
   448	only $m \mid q$.  The cited route therefore does not establish the
   449	polynomial-pair lemma, nor the soundness of the Pauli basis test that
   450	depends on it, beyond $m = 1$ and $q \ge 8$.  Independently of the
   451	divisibility, the import of the classical game's quantum soundness carries
   452	the two open verification obligations of
   453	Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations}: the asserted identity with the
   454	two-prover tensor-code test must be replaced by a reduction carrying a
   455	value bound, and the source's instantiation of the auxiliary parameter
   456	violates the theorem's lower bound at the small dimensions listed there.
   457	We do not assert that any conclusion is false: the underlying tensor-code
   458	soundness is insensitive to how the axis index is sampled, and both import
   459	obligations concern verification, not counterexample.  For the divisibility
   460	repair, the recommended candidate direction is direct index sampling ---

   180	\begin{theorem}[Main theorem; quantum soundness of the low individual degree test]\label{thm:main-formal}
   181	  Consider a projective strategy $(\psi, A^{\mathrm{A}},B^{\mathrm{A}},L^{\mathrm{A}},A^{\mathrm{B}},B^{\mathrm{B}},L^{\mathrm{B}})$

   187	  \end{equation*}

   189	\begin{enumerate}
   190	  \item (Consistency with~$A$):  On average over $\bu \sim \F_q^{m}$,
   191		  \begin{align*}
   192		  A^{\mathrm{A},u}_a \otimes I
   193		  	&\simeq_{\nu} I \otimes G^{\mathrm{B}}_{[g(u)=a]},\\
   194		I \otimes A^{\mathrm{B},u}_a
   195		  	&\simeq_{\nu}  G^{\mathrm{A}}_{[g(u)=a]} \ot I.
   196		  \end{align*}
   197	\item (Self-consistency):
   198		\begin{equation*}
   199		G^{\mathrm{A}}_g \ot I \simeq_{\nu} I \ot G^{\mathrm{B}}_g.
   200		\end{equation*}
   201	\end{enumerate}
   202	\end{theorem}
   203	
   204	We note that there is a tradeoff in \Cref{thm:main-formal} specified by the parameter~$k$.

   207	Thus, when applying this theorem, one must select~$k$ to balance these competing demands.
   208	Typically, choosing $k = \poly(m)$ should be more than sufficient for applications.

   396	
   397	\begin{definition}[Low-degree polynomial measurements]
   398	  \label{def:ld-meas}
   399	  Define $\polymeas{m}{d}{q}$ to be the set of POVM measurements whose outcomes
   400	  correspond to (individual) degree-$d$ polynomials of $m$ variables over
   401	  $\F_q$.
   402	  More generally, for an integer $\ldc$ and tuples $m=(m_1, m_2, \ldots,
   403	  m_\ldc)$, $d=(d_1, d_2, \ldots, d_\ldc)$ and $q=(q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_\ldc)$,
   404	  we let $\simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}$ be the set of measurements $G =
   405	  \{G_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots\,,\, g_\ldc}\}$ such that for $i\in\{1, 2, \ldots,
   406	  \ldc\}$, $g_i$ is a polynomial $g_i:\F_{q_i}^{m_i} \rightarrow
   407	  \F_{q_i}$ with individual degree $d_i$ (see \Cref{sec:ld-encoding} for a definition of individual degree). 
   408	\end{definition}
   409	
   410	Quantum soundness of a version of the classical low-degree test for polynomials of low \emph{total} degree was claimed
   411	in~\cite{natarajan2018low}, building on an analysis of a three-prover version of the test in~\cite{vidick2016three}. Unfortunately there is a gap in the soundness analysis of this test. For our construction we use the low individual degree test, whose quantum soundness is shown in~\cite{ML20} and generalized in~\cite{ji2021quantum}. We state the result in the form that is most directly useful for us, and show how the stated result follows from~\cite{ji2021quantum}.
   412	
   413	\begin{theorem}[Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low-degree test]
   414	  \label{lem:ld-soundness}
   415	  There exists a function $\delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc) = a (dm \ldc)^a (\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for universal constants $a\geq 1$ and $0<b\leq 1$ 
   416	such that the following
   417	  holds.
   418	  For all $\eps > 0$ and parameter tuple $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$, for all
   419	  projective strategies $(\psi,A,B)$ that succeed with probability at least
   420	  $1-\eps$ in the game $\game^\ld_\ldparams$, there exists measurements
   421	  \[G^w \in \simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}\] on $\mH_w$, for
   422	  $w\in\{\alice,\bob\}$, such that
   423	  \begin{equation*}
   424	    \begin{split}
   425	      A^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}
   426	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   427	      G^\bob_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}\;,\\
   428	      G^\alice_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}
   429	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   430				 B^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}\;,\\
   431	      G^\alice_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}
   432	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   433	      G^\bob_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}\;,
   434	    \end{split}
   435	  \end{equation*}
   436	  where $\delta_{\ld} = \delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc)$, 
   437	  and all three statements are with respect to the state $\ket{\psi}$.
   438	In addition, the first two approximations hold under the uniform distribution over $u\in \F_q^m$,
   439		whereas there is no question distribution associated with the third approximation.
   440	\end{theorem}

   442	\begin{proof}
   443	Let $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$
   444	where $m, d, \ldc \in \N$ are integers, $q \in \N$ is an admissible field size,
   445	and $m$ divides $q$. Let $\Sigma=\F_q$. Let $\code \subseteq \Sigma^q$ be the Reed-Solomon code with degree $d$. Explicitly, $\code$ is the set of all $(p(x_1),\ldots,p(x_n))$ where $p:\F_q\to\F_q$ is a univariate polynomial of degree at most $d$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ are an enumeration of $\F_q$. Then in the (standard) notation from~\cite{ji2021quantum} $\code$ is a linear $[q,d+1,n-d+1]_\Sigma$ code.
   446	
   447	Observe that the two-prover tensor code test, for the code $\code^{\otimes m}$, as described in~\cite[Figure 1 and Figure 2]{ji2021quantum}, is identical to the game $\game^\ld$ with parameters $\ldparams$ and $\ldc=1$, whose decider is presented in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider}. This is because 
   448	\begin{enumerate}
   449	\item The \emph{axis-parallel line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{axis-parallel lines test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with the only difference that in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} the roles of A and B are chosen uniformly at random. This is consistent with the two-prover variant of the tensor code test from~\cite[Section 4.1]{ji2021quantum}.
   450	\item The \emph{diagonal line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{subcube commutation test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with again the added symmetrization between players. 
   451	\item The \emph{consistency test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{synchronicity test} from~\cite[Figure 2]{ji2021quantum}.
   452	\end{enumerate}
   453	
   454	As a result,~\cite[Theorem 4.7]{ji2021quantum}, in which we choose the parameter $k$ as $k=m^3d$,  immediately yields \Cref{lem:ld-soundness}.
   455	
   456	To conclude it remains to extend the result to the case of general $\ldc$. This is done 
   457	via a standard reduction, following exactly the same steps as the derivation of Theorem 4.43 from Theorem 4.40 in~\cite{NW19}.
   458	\end{proof}

   253		Since $s$ is uniformly random in $\F_q$ and $m$ divides $q$ by assumption, we
   254	  have that $i$ is uniformly random between $\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ and therefore
   255	  $(u_0,s)$ specifies a uniformly random axis-parallel line $\line(u_0,e_i)$.

   261	\begin{lemma}
   262		\label{lem:dlnf}
   263		Consider the pair $(\line,u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the
   264	  tuple $((u_0,s,v),(u,0,0))$ from the CL distribution $\mu_{L_\DLine,L_\Point}$,
   265	  and let $\line = \line(u_0,v)$ where $i = \chi(s)$.
   266	  Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\F_q^m$ and $\line$ is a random
   267	  diagonal line that goes through $u$ and shares the first $i-1$ coordinates
   268	  with $u$, for uniformly random $i$.
   269	\end{lemma}

   271		The proof of this follows identically to \Cref{lem:alnf}.
   272	\end{proof}

   274	For later convenience we make the following definition. 
   275	
   276	\begin{definition}[Line-point distributions]
   277	        \label{def:line-point-dist}
   278	 The \emph{axis line-point distribution} $D_{\ALine}$ is the
   279	 distribution $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$ over pairs $(\ell=(u_0,e_i),u)$
   280	 (we omit the $0$ elements for simplicity). The \emph{diagonal
   281	   line-point distribution} $D_{\DLine}$ is the distribution
   282	 $\mu_{L_\DLine,L_\Point}$  over $(\ell=(u_0,s,v),u)$. The
   283	 \emph{line-point distribution} $D_{\Line}$ is the equal mixture of the axis-parallel line-point distribution and the diagonal line-point distribution.
   284	 In other words, a sample from $D_{\Line}$ is distributed as follows:
   285	 with probability $\tfrac{1}{2}$, output a sample from $D_{\ALine}$,
   286	 and with probability $\tfrac{1}{2}$, output a sample from $D_{\DLine}$.
   287	\end{definition}

   320	\paragraph{Decision procedure} The decision procedure $\decider^\ld$ for the
   321	game $\game^\ld$ is presented in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider}.
   322	The table at the top specifies a parsing scheme for the questions and answers,
   323	depending on the type of question.
   324	For example, when a player receives a question with type $\Point$, the question
   325	content $x$, a bit string of length $m \log q$, should be interpreted by the
   326	decision procedure and the players as an element of the vector space $\F_q^m$,
   327	as indicated in Section~\ref{sec:ff-representations}.
   328	Similarly the answer to a question with type $\Point$ is expected to be a bit
   329	string of length $\ldc \log q$, and is interpreted as an element of $\F_q^\ldc$.
   330	For questions with type $\ALine$, the question content is a $(m \log q + \log
   331	q)$-bit string, which is parsed as a pair $(u_0, s) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q$,
   332	which in turn can be interpreted as a specification for an axis-parallel line
   333	$\line(u_0,e_i)$ in $\F_q^m$ where $i = \chi(s)$, as described in
   334	\Cref{lem:alnf}.
   335	The answer is interpreted as the description of $\ldc$ degree-$d$ univariate
   336	polynomials defined on the line $\line(u_0,e_i)$, each polynomial given by a
   337	list of $d+1$ coefficients.
   338	For questions with type $\DLine$, the question content is a $(2m \log q + \log
   339	q)$-bit string, which is parsed as a triple $(u_0, s, v) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q
   340	\times \F_q^m$ that specifies a diagonal line $\line(u_0,v')$ where $v' =
   341	\pi_{i-1}(v)$ as described in \Cref{lem:dlnf}.
   342	The answer is interpreted as the description of $\ldc$ degree-$md$ univariate
   343	polynomials defined on the line $\line(u_0,v')$.
   344	If the answers returned by the players do not fit this format the decision
   345	procedure rejects.

blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:123:	The source states the two line-versus-point clauses with ``the'' $t \in \F_q$ such that $x_{\overline w} = u_0 + t v$. When the direction is nonzero and $x_{\overline w}$ lies on the line, exactly one such $t$ exists and the formulation above agrees with the source. But zero directions occur: Definition~\ref{def:line} explicitly permits them, and the question distribution of Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution} produces $\mathsf{DLine}$ questions with $v' = \pi_{i-1}(v) = 0$ with positive probability, namely whenever the last $m - i + 1$ coordinates of $v$ vanish. In that case $\ell(u_0, 0) = \{u_0\}$, every $t \in \F_q$ satisfies $x_{\overline w} = u_0 + t v'$ when $x_{\overline w} = u_0$, and the source clause does not determine acceptance for a nonconstant answer polynomial. The universal quantification over $t$ adopted in Definition~\ref{def:ld-win-predicate} makes the predicate a well-defined function of its arguments; it accepts vacuously when no such $t$ exists, a case the question distribution never produces. Completeness is unaffected: the restriction of a polynomial $g$ to the singleton line $\ell(u_0,0)$, expressed through the parameterization $t \mapsto u_0 + t \cdot 0$, is the constant polynomial with value $g(u_0)$, which passes the check for every $t$. Soundness is likewise unaffected: zero directions occur with probability at most $2/(mq)$, so any acceptance convention on this event changes success probabilities by at most that amount; the game-correspondence obligation enumerated in the proof of Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness} accounts for this event explicitly, and an error of this shape is absorbed into the universal constants of $\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}$.
blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex-124-\end{remark}

   301	(form~4 above).  This removes the divisibility obstruction and nothing

   307	
   308	The relation to the present game when $m' \mid q$ must moreover be proved
   309	at the level of games, not merely of question distributions, because the
   310	two games have different question alphabets: an $\mathsf{ALine}$ question
   311	of the $\chi$-based game is a pair $(u_0, s)$ and a $\mathsf{DLine}$
   312	question a triple $(u_0, s, v')$, so a strategy may select different
   313	measurements for seeds $s \ne s'$ with $\chi(s) = \chi(s')$, and equality
   314	of the induced laws of the geometric data does not by itself transport
   315	such a strategy.  The transport layer decomposes into the following
   316	obligations, none of which is carried out here.
   317	\begin{itemize}
   318	  \item \emph{Distribution lemma.}  When $m' \mid q$, the image of the
   319	  conditionally linear question distribution under the parsing map
   320	  $(u_0,s) \mapsto (u_0,\chi(s))$, $(u_0,s,v') \mapsto (u_0,\chi(s),v')$
   321	  is the direct distribution, and conditioned on the parsed question the
   322	  seed is uniform on the class $\chi^{-1}(i)$, independently of everything
   323	  else.
   324	  \item \emph{Parsing pullback.}  A strategy for the directly indexed game
   325	  composed with the parsing map is a seed-oblivious strategy for the
   326	  $\chi$-based game.  Since the win predicate depends on the question only
   327	  through the parsed data, and a seed-oblivious strategy answers
   328	  identically across each fiber --- in particular on the synchronicity
   329	  branches, where both players hold the same seed --- the value should be
   330	  preserved exactly on every branch, and projectivity is preserved.  This
   331	  is the direction the combining subtree needs.
   332	  \item \emph{Seed-fiber averaging: what it preserves and what it does
   333	  not.}  In the opposite direction, average each line measurement over its
   334	  seed fiber: attach to a direct question $(u_0,i)$, respectively
   335	  $(u_0,i,v')$, the average over uniform $s \in \chi^{-1}(i)$ of the
   336	  measurements attached to $(u_0,s)$, respectively $(u_0,s,v')$, leaving
   337	  the points measurements unchanged.  By the conditional uniformity of the
   338	  seed this preserves the value of every \emph{line-versus-point} branch
   339	  exactly: there the paired question carries no seed, so the branch value
   340	  is an average over the fiber of per-seed values, which the averaged
   341	  measurement computes.  It does \emph{not} preserve the synchronicity
   342	  branches.  There both players hold the same seed, so the $\chi$-based
   343	  branch value is the diagonal average
   344	  $\E_{s}\sum_f \langle M^{(u_0,s)}_f \ot \widetilde M^{(u_0,s)}_f
   345	  \rangle$, while the averaged strategy realizes the double average
   346	  $\E_{s,s'}\sum_f \langle M^{(u_0,s)}_f \ot \widetilde M^{(u_0,s')}_f
   347	  \rangle$ over independent seeds in the fiber; the two differ whenever
   348	  the players' measurements vary across a fiber in a correlated way (if
   349	  both apply a common seed-dependent relabelling, every diagonal term is
   350	  large and the cross terms are not), and neither quantity dominates the
   351	  other in general.  An earlier revision of this note claimed that the
   352	  averaging preserves the exact value, and with it synchronicity; that
   353	  claim was wrong and is withdrawn.  What needs proof is control of the
   354	  synchronicity branches under de-seeding.  Candidate approaches: show
   355	  that a strategy of value $1-\eps$ in the $\chi$-based game is, with
   356	  polynomial loss, close to a seed-oblivious one; or state form~4 with a
   357	  synchronicity hypothesis in the doubled-average form and re-derive it on
   358	  the tensor-code side.  Choosing and proving one of these is an open
   359	  obligation.
   360	  \item \emph{Projectivity round trip.}  The averaged strategy is a POVM
   361	  strategy even when the given one is projective, while the imported
   362	  theorem, like the present one, takes projective strategies.  The
   363	  intended round trip is: dilate the averaged strategy to a projective one
   364	  (Naimark preserves all product correlations
   365	  $\langle X \ot Y \rangle$ of the given strategy against the dilated
   366	  state --- hence the value of every branch the averaging preserved ---
   367	  but nothing restores the diagonal seed correlations once the averaging
   368	  has been performed); apply form~4; and compress the resulting polynomial
   369	  measurement along the dilation isometry back to a POVM in the required
   370	  measurement class on the original space.  That this compression
   371	  preserves the consistency conclusions must itself be proved; it is
   372	  stated here as an obligation, not established.  (Alternatively, form~4
   373	  may be stated for POVM strategies outright, moving the dilation inside
   374	  the import.)
   375	\end{itemize}
   376	
   377	The combining subtree would then be reread with the direct distribution
   378	and the directly indexed game at dimension $2m+2$: every statement becomes
   379	well defined for all admissible tuples, and the expectation is that the
   380	proofs survive unchanged, because the measurements constructed there are
   381	indexed by the geometric data --- points, lines, and polynomials on them
   382	--- and so constitute a strategy for the directly indexed game outright,
   383	with no fiber averaging.  Verifying, lemma by lemma, that those proofs use
   384	only the laws of the sampled objects and never the conditional linearity
   385	of the sampling is part of this direction's obligations.  This follows the
   386	subtree protocol for a definition-level mismatch: the definition is
   387	corrected at the lowest point rather than each downstream lemma acquiring

   397	with no index encoding into $\F_q$.

   399	\paragraph{Padding the dimension.}
   400	Alternatively, embed the combined polynomial into
   401	$\mathrm{ideg}_{d,\bar m}(\F_q)$ for $\bar m = 4m$, the least power of two

   403	$\bar m \mid q$ holds whenever $q \ge 4m$, and the existing game applies at

 # The directly indexed low-degree game
 
 The low-degree game used by the Pauli-basis combining argument is needed in
 dimension `2 * m + 2`.  The existing conditionally linear game represents a
 coordinate index by an equally sized fiber in the scalar field and therefore
 requires the dimension to divide the field size.  This file gives the separate
 directly indexed variant which samples that index directly.
 
 The geometric line carrier records the sampled coordinate, and line evaluation
 uses an `Option` outcome rather than assigning a value when a point does not
 determine one.  The game retains the point, axis-line, and diagonal-line answer
 formats and the nine ordered type branches of the original low-degree game.
 
 The `Transport` modules relate the direct game to the seed-indexed game and to
 the mature low individual degree test interface: `Transport.Correspondence`
 identifies coordinates, answers, and the question law of the two QPBT
 presentations; `Transport.SeedFiber` dilates a seed-indexed strategy to a
 direct strategy by a correlated residue register, and `Transport.SeedFiberValue`
 shows that the dilation preserves the value exactly; `Transport.Questions`
 reads mature lines as canonical direct questions and rebases direct answers;
 `Transport.Strategy` reads one coordinate of a projective direct strategy as a
-mature `ProjStrat`, with exact Born-weight formulas for both adapters; and
+mature `ProjStrat`, with exact Born-weight formulas for both adapters;
+`Transport.Consistency` reexpresses the three single-polynomial LDT consistency
+relations in direct coordinates, the first two at a fixed tuple coordinate; and
 `Transport.BranchComparison`, `Transport.DiagonalRecursion`, and
 `Transport.PassConversion` convert a value bound of the direct game into the
 pass hypothesis of the mature low individual degree theorem for every
 coordinate strategy.  `GameValue` supplies the rejection calculus relating the
 direct value to the mature branch weights.
 
 ## References
 
 The underlying game is `def:ld-game` in
 `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, with source origin
 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
 The need for the directly indexed repair in Chapter 15 is explained around
 `rem:qld-4-7-divisibility` in
 `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1257-1293` and in
 `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`.
 -/

    87	/-- Turn a coefficient vector into its polynomial of degree at most `n`. -/
    88	private noncomputable def coefficientPolynomial
    89	    {K : Type*} [Field K] (n : ℕ) (c : Fin (n + 1) → K) : Polynomial K :=
    90	  ((Polynomial.degreeLTEquiv K (n + 1)).symm c).1
    91	
    92	private theorem coefficientPolynomial_degree_le
    93	    {K : Type*} [Field K] (n : ℕ) (c : Fin (n + 1) → K) :
    94	    (coefficientPolynomial n c).natDegree ≤ n := by
    95	  let p := (Polynomial.degreeLTEquiv K (n + 1)).symm c
    96	  have hp : p.1 ∈ Polynomial.degreeLE K n := by
    97	    rw [← Polynomial.degreeLT_succ_eq_degreeLE]
    98	    exact p.2
    99	  have hdegree : p.1.degree ≤ n := Polynomial.mem_degreeLE.mp hp
   100	  by_cases hzero : p.1 = 0
   101	  · simp [coefficientPolynomial, p, hzero]
   102	  · exact Polynomial.natDegree_le_iff_degree_le.mpr hdegree
   103	
   104	@[simp] private theorem coefficientPolynomial_coeff
   105	    {K : Type*} [Field K] (n : ℕ) (c : Fin (n + 1) → K)
   106	    (i : Fin (n + 1)) :
   107	    (coefficientPolynomial n c).coeff i = c i := by
   108	  exact congrFun ((Polynomial.degreeLTEquiv K (n + 1)).apply_symm_apply c) i
   109	
   110	private theorem coefficientPolynomial_eval
   111	    {K : Type*} [Field K] (n : ℕ) (c : Fin (n + 1) → K) (t : K) :
   112	    (coefficientPolynomial n c).eval t = evalCoefficient c t := by
   113	  simpa [coefficientPolynomial, evalCoefficient] using
   114	    (Polynomial.eval_eq_sum_degreeLTEquiv
   115	      (((Polynomial.degreeLTEquiv K (n + 1)).symm c).2) t)

   117	/-- Direct axis-line coefficients are equivalent to mature bounded axis-line
   118	polynomials over the fixed field model. -/
   119	noncomputable def directAxisAnswerEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   120	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   121	    DirectDegPoly D D.d ≃ AxisLinePolynomial D.toLDTParameters := by
   122	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   123	  refine
   124	    { toFun := fun c =>
   125	        { poly := coefficientPolynomial D.d c
   126	          degreeBounded := coefficientPolynomial_degree_le D.d c }
   127	      invFun := fun f i => f.poly.coeff i
   128	      left_inv := ?_
   129	      right_inv := ?_ }
   130	  · intro c
   131	    funext i
   132	    exact coefficientPolynomial_coeff D.d c i
   133	  · intro f
   134	    apply AxisLinePolynomial.ext
   135	    apply linePolynomial_coeff_fin_injective D.toLDTParameters
   136	      (coefficientPolynomial_degree_le D.d fun i => f.poly.coeff i)
   137	      f.degreeBounded
   138	    intro i
   139	    exact coefficientPolynomial_coeff D.d (fun j => f.poly.coeff j) i

   141	/-- Direct diagonal-line coefficients are equivalent to mature bounded
   142	diagonal-line polynomials over the fixed field model. -/
   143	noncomputable def directDiagonalAnswerEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   144	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   145	    DirectDegPoly D (D.m * D.d) ≃ DiagonalLinePolynomial D.toLDTParameters := by
   146	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   147	  refine
   148	    { toFun := fun c =>
   149	        { poly := coefficientPolynomial (D.m * D.d) c
   150	          degreeBounded := coefficientPolynomial_degree_le (D.m * D.d) c }
   151	      invFun := fun f i => f.poly.coeff i
   152	      left_inv := ?_
   153	      right_inv := ?_ }
   154	  · intro c
   155	    funext i
   156	    exact coefficientPolynomial_coeff (D.m * D.d) c i
   157	  · intro f
   158	    apply DiagonalLinePolynomial.ext
   159	    apply linePolynomial_coeff_fin_injective D.toLDTParameters
   160	      (coefficientPolynomial_degree_le (D.m * D.d) fun i => f.poly.coeff i)
   161	      f.degreeBounded
   162	    intro i
   163	    exact coefficientPolynomial_coeff (D.m * D.d) (fun j => f.poly.coeff j) i

   165	/-- Coefficient evaluation agrees with evaluation of the corresponding mature
   166	axis-line polynomial. -/
   167	theorem directAxisAnswerEquiv_apply (D : DirectLdParams)
   168	    (c : DirectDegPoly D D.d) (t : DirectScalarQ D) :
   169	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel

   171	      directScalarEquiv D (evalCoefficient c t) := by
   172	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   173	  simp only [directAxisAnswerEquiv, AxisLinePolynomial.toFun,
   174	    evalLinePolynomialModel]
   175	  rw [show decodeScalar (directScalarEquiv D t) = t by
   176	    exact (FieldModel.equiv (q := D.q)).symm_apply_apply t]
   177	  change encodeScalar ((coefficientPolynomial D.d c).eval t) =
   178	    directScalarEquiv D (evalCoefficient c t)
   179	  exact congrArg (FieldModel.equiv (q := D.q))
   180	    (coefficientPolynomial_eval D.d c t)

   183	diagonal-line polynomial. -/

   185	    (c : DirectDegPoly D (D.m * D.d)) (t : DirectScalarQ D) :
   186	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   187	    directDiagonalAnswerEquiv D c (directScalarEquiv D t) =
   188	      directScalarEquiv D (evalCoefficient c t) := by
   189	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   190	  simp only [directDiagonalAnswerEquiv, DiagonalLinePolynomial.toFun,
   191	    evalLinePolynomialModel]
   192	  rw [show decodeScalar (directScalarEquiv D t) = t by
   193	    exact (FieldModel.equiv (q := D.q)).symm_apply_apply t]
   194	  change encodeScalar ((coefficientPolynomial (D.m * D.d) c).eval t) =
   195	    directScalarEquiv D (evalCoefficient c t)

   197	    (coefficientPolynomial_eval (D.m * D.d) c t)

     6	# Seed-fiber dilation for the directly indexed low-degree game
     7	
     8	This module dilates a seed-indexed low-degree strategy by a maximally
     9	correlated residue register.  Block-diagonal projective measurements retain
    10	arbitrary dependence on the seed within each `chiIndex` fiber.

    13

    29	/-- Relabel a matrix measurement along an equivalence of outcome alphabets. -/
    30	noncomputable def matrixMeasurementTransport
    31	    {alpha beta iota : Type*}
    32	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype beta] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    33	    (e : alpha ≃ beta) (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota) :
    34	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement beta iota :=
    35	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
    36	    (fun b => M.effect (e.symm b))
    37	    (fun b => M.pos (e.symm b))
    38	    (by
    39	      calc
    40	        ∑ b, M.effect (e.symm b) = ∑ a, M.effect a :=
    41	          Equiv.sum_comp e.symm M.effect
    42	        _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one)
    43	
    44	@[simp] theorem matrixMeasurementTransport_effect
    45	    {alpha beta iota : Type*}
    46	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype beta] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    47	    (e : alpha ≃ beta) (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
    48	    (b : beta) :
    49	    (matrixMeasurementTransport e M).effect b = M.effect (e.symm b) :=
    50	  rfl
    51	
    52	/-- Relabeling a projective matrix measurement preserves projectivity. -/
    53	theorem matrixMeasurementTransport_isProjective
    54	    {alpha beta iota : Type*}
    55	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype beta] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    56	    (e : alpha ≃ beta) (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
    57	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) :
    58	    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (matrixMeasurementTransport e M) :=
    59	  fun b => hM (e.symm b)
    60	
    61	/-- Assemble a family of matrix measurements as diagonal blocks indexed by a
    62	finite classical register. -/
    63	noncomputable def blockDiagonalMeasurement
    64	    {alpha iota block : Type*}
    65	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    66	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block]
    67	    (M : block → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota) :
    68	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha (iota × block) :=
    69	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
    70	    (fun a => Matrix.blockDiagonal fun r => (M r).effect a)
    71	    (fun a => Matrix.blockDiagonal_nonneg
    72	      (fun r => (M r).effect a) (fun r => (M r).pos a))
    73	    (by
    74	      ext ⟨i, r⟩ ⟨j, s⟩
    75	      simp only [Matrix.sum_apply, Matrix.blockDiagonal_apply]
    76	      by_cases hrs : r = s
    77	      · subst s
    78	        simp only [if_pos]
    79	        calc
    80	          ∑ x, (M r).effect x i j = (1 : Matrix iota iota ℂ) i j :=
    81	            by
    82	              simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply] using
    83	                congrFun (congrFun (M r).sum_eq_one i) j
    84	          _ = (1 : Matrix (iota × block) (iota × block) ℂ)
    85	              (i, r) (j, r) := by
    86	                change (if i = j then 1 else 0) =
    87	                  (if (i, r) = (j, r) then 1 else 0)
    88	                simp
    89	      · simp [hrs])
    90	
    91	@[simp] theorem blockDiagonalMeasurement_effect
    92	    {alpha iota block : Type*}
    93	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    94	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block]
    95	    (M : block → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
    96	    (a : alpha) :
    97	    (blockDiagonalMeasurement M).effect a =
    98	      Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a) :=
    99	  rfl

   101	/-- A block-diagonal family of projective measurements is projective. -/
   102	theorem blockDiagonalMeasurement_isProjective
   103	    {alpha iota block : Type*}
   104	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   105	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block]
   106	    (M : block → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
   107	    (hM : ∀ r, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (M r)) :
   108	    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (blockDiagonalMeasurement M) := by
   109	  intro a
   110	  constructor
   111	  · change Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a) *
   112	        Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a) =
   113	      Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a)
   114	    rw [← Matrix.blockDiagonal_mul]
   115	    congr 1
   116	    funext r
   117	    exact (hM r a).isIdempotentElem.eq
   118	  · change (Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a))ᴴ =
   119	      Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a)
   120	    rw [Matrix.blockDiagonal_conjTranspose]
   121	    congr 1
   122	    funext r
   123	    exact (hM r a).isSelfAdjoint.star_eq

   125	/-! ## The correlated residue state -/
   126	
   127	/-- The normalized maximally correlated state on the common seed-fiber
   128	residue. -/
   129	noncomputable def seedResidueAncilla (L : LdParams) :
   130	    EuclideanSpace ℂ
   131	      (Fin (L.q / L.m) × Fin (L.q / L.m)) := by
   132	  letI : Nonempty (Fin (L.q / L.m)) :=
   133	    Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp L.seedFiberCard_pos
   134	  exact eprState (Fin (L.q / L.m))
   135	
   136	/-- The seed-residue ancilla has unit norm. -/
   137	theorem seedResidueAncilla_norm (L : LdParams) :
   138	    ‖seedResidueAncilla L‖ = 1 := by
   139	  letI : Nonempty (Fin (L.q / L.m)) :=
   140	    Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp L.seedFiberCard_pos
   141	  exact eprState_norm (Fin (L.q / L.m))
   142	
   143	/-- Reindexing Euclidean coordinates along an equivalence preserves norm. -/
   144	theorem reindexState_norm_eq
   145	    {iota kappa : Type*}
   146	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   147	    [Fintype kappa] [DecidableEq kappa]
   148	    (e : iota ≃ kappa) (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
   149	    ‖reindexState e psi‖ = ‖psi‖ := by
   150	  rw [← sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _)]
   151	  rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq, EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq]
   152	  change (∑ j : kappa, ‖psi (e.symm j)‖ ^ 2) = ∑ i : iota, ‖psi i‖ ^ 2
   153	  exact e.symm.sum_comp (fun i => ‖psi i‖ ^ 2)
   154	
   155	/-- The coordinate tensor of two Euclidean vectors has the product norm. -/
   156	theorem vecTensor_norm_eq
   157	    {iota kappa : Type*}
   158	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   159	    [Fintype kappa] [DecidableEq kappa]
   160	    (u : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ kappa) :
   161	    ‖vecTensor u v‖ = ‖u‖ * ‖v‖ := by
   162	  rw [← sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (mul_nonneg (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _))]
   163	  rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq, mul_pow, EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq,
   164	    EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq]
   165	  change (∑ p : iota × kappa, ‖u p.1 * v p.2‖ ^ 2) =
   166	    (∑ i : iota, ‖u i‖ ^ 2) * ∑ j : kappa, ‖v j‖ ^ 2
   167	  simp only [norm_mul, mul_pow]
   168	  rw [← Finset.univ_product_univ, Finset.sum_product, Finset.sum_mul]
   169	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   170	  intro i hi
   171	  rw [Finset.mul_sum]

   173	/-- Tensor the original strategy state with the maximally correlated residue
   174	state and shuffle the factors back into the two local carriers. -/
   175	noncomputable def seedFiberLiftedState
   176	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (L : LdParams) :
   177	    EuclideanSpace ℂ
   178	      ((S.ιA × Fin (L.q / L.m)) × (S.ιB × Fin (L.q / L.m))) :=
   179	  reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor S.ψ (seedResidueAncilla L))

   181	/-- The correlated seed-fiber lift preserves normalization of the strategy
   182	state. -/
   183	theorem seedFiberLiftedState_norm
   184	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (L : LdParams) :
   185	    ‖seedFiberLiftedState S L‖ = 1 := by
   186	  rw [seedFiberLiftedState, reindexState_norm_eq, vecTensor_norm_eq,
   187	    S.ψ_norm, seedResidueAncilla_norm, one_mul]

   189	/-! ## From the seed-indexed game to the direct game -/
   190	
   191	/-- The seed-indexed question selected in one residue block of a direct
   192	question.  Applying `ldCL` ensures that irrelevant ambient coordinates are
   193	canonicalized exactly as in the source game. -/
   194	noncomputable def seededLdQuestion (L : LdParams)
   195	    (q : DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams)
   196	    (residue : Fin (L.q / L.m)) : LdQuestion L :=
   197	  (q.1, ldCL L q.1 (ldSpaceOfDirectResidue L q.2 residue))
   198	
   199	/-- Dilate a strategy for the seed-indexed low-degree game to the directly
   200	indexed game.  The two local carriers receive correlated copies of the seed
   201	residue, and each measurement is block diagonal in that residue. -/
   202	noncomputable def ldStrategyToDirect (L : LdParams)
   203	    (S : Strategy (ldGame L)) : Strategy (directLdGame L.toDirectLdParams) where
   204	  ιA := S.ιA × Fin (L.q / L.m)
   205	  ιB := S.ιB × Fin (L.q / L.m)
   206	  ψ := seedFiberLiftedState S L
   207	  ψ_norm := seedFiberLiftedState_norm S L
   208	  A q := blockDiagonalMeasurement fun residue =>
   209	    matrixMeasurementTransport (ldDirectAnswerEquiv L)
   210	      (S.A (seededLdQuestion L q residue))
   211	  B q := blockDiagonalMeasurement fun residue =>
   212	    matrixMeasurementTransport (ldDirectAnswerEquiv L)
   213	      (S.B (seededLdQuestion L q residue))

   215	/-- Projectivity is preserved by the correlated seed-fiber dilation. -/
   216	theorem ldStrategyToDirect_isProjective (L : LdParams)
   217	    (S : Strategy (ldGame L)) (hS : S.IsProjective) :
   218	    (ldStrategyToDirect L S).IsProjective := by
   219	  constructor
   220	  · intro q
   221	    apply blockDiagonalMeasurement_isProjective
   222	    intro residue
   223	    apply matrixMeasurementTransport_isProjective
   224	    exact hS.1 (seededLdQuestion L q residue)
   225	  · intro q
   226	    apply blockDiagonalMeasurement_isProjective
   227	    intro residue
   228	    apply matrixMeasurementTransport_isProjective
   229	    exact hS.2 (seededLdQuestion L q residue)

   244	    (answer : DirectLdAnswer L.toDirectLdParams) :

   251	/-- A direct question reconstructed in a residue block parses back to its

   253	theorem parse_seededLdQuestion (L : LdParams)

This bridge is exactly the tensor-placement bookkeeping needed by the formal completion proof. docs/reports/issue-930-session48-making-projective-audit.md-91-The completion theorem `completingToMeasurement` matches the paper proposition after making those hypotheses explicit. It assumes a measurement `A`, a submeasurement `B`, a closeness bound `A≈_δ B`, and bipartite strong self-consistency of `A` at level `ζ`, and returns the canonical completion with error `2δ+4√δ+2ζ` (`CompletionTransfer.lean:229-254`). The structural helper `completeAtOutcomeProj` proves that completing a projective submeasurement by adding the residual mass at one outcome gives a projective measurement (`Completion.lean:17-25`). This is the exact structural fact used by the projectivization chain.

   101	\begin{definition}[Win predicate of the classical low individual degree game]\label{def:ld-win-predicate}
   102		\uses{def:ld-game, def:ld-question-distribution, def:line, def:polyfunc}
   103		Fix $\mathsf{ldparams} = (q,m,d,k)$. Answers in the game $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{ld}}_{\mathsf{ldparams}}$ take the following forms, depending on the question type; answers not of the prescribed form are rejected.
   104		\begin{itemize}
   105			\item Type $\mathsf{Point}$, question content $u \in \F_q^m$: the answer is an element of $\F_q^k$.
   106			\item Type $\mathsf{ALine}$, question content $(u_0,s) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q$, specifying the axis-parallel line $\ell(u_0,e_i)$ with $i = \chi(s)$: the answer is a $k$-tuple $(f_1,\ldots,f_k)$ of univariate polynomials $f_j\colon \F_q \to \F_q$ of degree at most $d$, each given by its $d+1$ coefficients.
   107			\item Type $\mathsf{DLine}$, question content $(u_0,s,v) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q \times \F_q^m$, specifying the diagonal line $\ell(u_0,v')$ with $v' = \pi_{i-1}(v)$ and $i = \chi(s)$: the answer is a $k$-tuple of univariate polynomials of degree at most $md$.
   108		\end{itemize}
   109		The win predicate $D^{\mathrm{ld}} = D^{\mathrm{ld}}_{\mathsf{ldparams}}$ is the function of the tuple $(t_{\mathrm A}, x_{\mathrm A}, t_{\mathrm B}, x_{\mathrm B}, a_{\mathrm A}, a_{\mathrm B})$ determined by the following clauses, evaluated for $w \in \{\mathrm A,\mathrm B\}$; in all cases where no action is indicated, the predicate accepts.
   110		\begin{enumerate}
   111			\item (\textbf{Consistency test}) If $t_{\mathrm A} = t_{\mathrm B}$, accept if and only if $a_{\mathrm A} = a_{\mathrm B}$.
   112			% The source phrases both clauses with "the" t such that x = u_0 + tv; that phrase
   113			% does not determine t on diagonal questions with direction v' = 0, which the
   114			% question distribution samples with positive probability. The universal
   115			% quantification over t used here is the local correction; see the remark below.
   116			\item (\textbf{Axis-parallel line-versus-point test}) If $t_w = \mathsf{ALine}$ and $t_{\overline w} = \mathsf{Point}$, accept if and only if $f_j(t) = (a_{\overline w})_j$ for all $j \in \{1,2,\ldots,k\}$ and all $t \in \F_q$ such that $x_{\overline w} = u_0 + t e_i$, where $i = \chi(s)$.
   117			\item (\textbf{Diagonal line-versus-point test}) If $t_w = \mathsf{DLine}$ and $t_{\overline w} = \mathsf{Point}$, accept if and only if $f_j(t) = (a_{\overline w})_j$ for all $j \in \{1,2,\ldots,k\}$ and all $t \in \F_q$ such that $x_{\overline w} = u_0 + t v'$, where $v' = \pi_{i-1}(v)$ and $i = \chi(s)$.
   118		\end{enumerate}
   119		The game $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{ld}}_{\mathsf{ldparams}}$ is the typed game with type set $\mathcal T^{\mathrm{ld}}$, the question distribution of Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution}, and win predicate $D^{\mathrm{ld}}_{\mathsf{ldparams}}$.
   120	\end{definition}
   121	
   122	\begin{remark}[Diagonal questions with zero direction]\label{rem:ld-win-zero-direction}
   123		The source states the two line-versus-point clauses with ``the'' $t \in \F_q$ such that $x_{\overline w} = u_0 + t v$. When the direction is nonzero and $x_{\overline w}$ lies on the line, exactly one such $t$ exists and the formulation above agrees with the source. But zero directions occur: Definition~\ref{def:line} explicitly permits them, and the question distribution of Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution} produces $\mathsf{DLine}$ questions with $v' = \pi_{i-1}(v) = 0$ with positive probability, namely whenever the last $m - i + 1$ coordinates of $v$ vanish. In that case $\ell(u_0, 0) = \{u_0\}$, every $t \in \F_q$ satisfies $x_{\overline w} = u_0 + t v'$ when $x_{\overline w} = u_0$, and the source clause does not determine acceptance for a nonconstant answer polynomial. The universal quantification over $t$ adopted in Definition~\ref{def:ld-win-predicate} makes the predicate a well-defined function of its arguments; it accepts vacuously when no such $t$ exists, a case the question distribution never produces. Completeness is unaffected: the restriction of a polynomial $g$ to the singleton line $\ell(u_0,0)$, expressed through the parameterization $t \mapsto u_0 + t \cdot 0$, is the constant polynomial with value $g(u_0)$, which passes the check for every $t$. Soundness is likewise unaffected: zero directions occur with probability at most $2/(mq)$, so any acceptance convention on this event changes success probabilities by at most that amount; the game-correspondence obligation enumerated in the proof of Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness} accounts for this event explicitly, and an error of this shape is absorbed into the universal constants of $\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}$.
   124	\end{remark}

+@[simp] theorem directPointQuestionOf_directPointEquiv
+    (D : DirectLdParams) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :
+    directPointQuestionOf D (directPointEquiv D u) =
+      directLdPointQuestionOf D u := by
+  unfold directPointQuestionOf ldtPointToDirect
+  rw [(directPointEquiv D).symm_apply_apply]
+
+/-- LDT points associated with direct parameters have a canonical zero
+witness. -/
+instance directLdtPointNonempty (D : DirectLdParams) :
+    Nonempty (Point D.toLDTParameters) :=
+  ⟨fun _ => ⟨0, D.toLDTParameters.hq⟩⟩
+
+/-- The LDT scalar readout is the direct coordinate readout followed by
+the scalar coding equivalence. -/
+@[simp] theorem directPointAnswerReadout_eq
+    (D : DirectLdParams) (r : Fin D.k) (answer : DirectLdAnswer D) :
+    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+    directPointAnswerReadout D r answer =
+      directScalarEquiv D (directLdPointValuesOrZero D answer r) := by
+  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+  cases answer <;> rfl
+
+/-- At corresponding points and scalar outcomes, the LDT point effect is
+the effect of the direct point measurement followed by coordinate projection. -/
+theorem directCoordinatePointMeasurement_effect_transport
+    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
+    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k)
+    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (a : DirectScalarQ D) :
+    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+    (((directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).pointMeasurementA
+      (directPointEquiv D u)).outcome (directScalarEquiv D a)) =
+      ((S.A (directLdPointQuestionOf D u)).postprocess
+        (fun answer => directLdPointValuesOrZero D answer r)).effect a := by
+  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+  classical
+  simp only [directCoordinateProjStrat, directCoordinatePointMeasurement,
+    directLdGame,
+    ProjMeas.postprocess, SubMeas.postprocess_outcome,
+    matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas_outcome,
+    directPointQuestionOf_directPointEquiv,
+    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
+  congr 1
+  ext answer
+  rw [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_filter]
+  simp only [Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
+  simpa only [directPointAnswerReadout_eq] using
+    (directScalarEquiv D).injective.eq_iff
+
+/-- Bob's point effects satisfy the same direct-to-LDT readout identity. -/
+theorem directCoordinatePointMeasurementB_effect_transport
+    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
+    (hS : S.IsProjective) (r : Fin D.k)
+    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (a : DirectScalarQ D) :
+    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+    (((directCoordinateProjStrat D S hS r).pointMeasurementB
+      (directPointEquiv D u)).outcome (directScalarEquiv D a)) =
+      ((S.B (directLdPointQuestionOf D u)).postprocess
+        (fun answer => directLdPointValuesOrZero D answer r)).effect a := by
+  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
+  classical
+  simp only [directCoordinateProjStrat, directCoordinatePointMeasurement,
+    directLdGame,
+    ProjMeas.postprocess, SubMeas.postprocess_outcome,
+    matrixMeasurementToLDTProjMeas_outcome,
+    directPointQuestionOf_directPointEquiv,
+    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
+  congr 1
+  ext answer
+  rw [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_filter]
+  simp only [Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
+  simpa only [directPointAnswerReadout_eq] using
+    (directScalarEquiv D).injective.eq_iff
+
+/-- Alice's direct point measurement followed by projection to coordinate
+`r`. -/
+noncomputable def directPointCoordinateMeasurementA
+    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
+    (r : Fin D.k) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :
+    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (DirectScalarQ D) S.ιA :=
+  (S.A (directLdPointQuestionOf D u)).postprocess
+    (fun answer => directLdPointValuesOrZero D answer r)
+
+/-- Bob's direct point measurement followed by projection to coordinate
+`r`. -/
+noncomputable def directPointCoordinateMeasurementB
+    (D : DirectLdParams) (S : Strategy (directLdGame D))
+    (r : Fin D.k) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :
+    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (DirectScalarQ D) S.ιB :=
+  (S.B (directLdPointQuestionOf D u)).postprocess
+    (fun answer => directLdPointValuesOrZero D answer r)
+
+/-- Evaluate a transported LDT polynomial measurement at a direct point. -/

+          MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (DirectScalarQ D) iota := by

405	**Smell.** Lean code re-declares or re-proves something that already lives
   406	in Mathlib, or builds a tower of custom lemmas that never bottom out in
   407	Mathlib / Lean core. The proof "works" only because the internal custom
   408	statements are compatible with each other — it is a closed ecosystem that
   409	doesn't ground in the reference library.
   410	
   411	This is the "scaffolding that blocks real formalization" section of
   412	[`project_conventions.md`](./project_conventions.md) in concrete examples. The two
   413	flavours:
   414	
   415	1. **Re-proving Mathlib.** Writing `private lemma my_add_comm : a + b = b + a`
   416	   when `add_comm` exists.
   417	2. **Custom types that shadow Mathlib.** Defining `MyMeasurement` instead of
   418	   using `MeasureTheory.Measure`, `MyMatrix` instead of `Matrix`,
   419	   `MyHermitian` instead of `Matrix.IsHermitian`. The custom version may be
   420	   definitionally equal to (or coercible from) the Mathlib version, but if
   421	   it isn't, every consumer must reprove everything.
   422	
   423	### Why it's bad
   424	
   425	1. The duplicated statements aren't audited by Mathlib's community, so they
   426	   may be subtly wrong (wrong edge case, wrong universe, wrong typeclass).
   427	2. When the real Mathlib proof is needed (for a key gap lemma), the custom
   428	   tower must be rewritten to interoperate — often via a painful coercion
   429	   layer that reintroduces every fact.
   430	3. Hides real Mathlib gaps. If we decline to use Mathlib because "our
   431	   version is simpler," the gap never gets filed against Mathlib.
   432	
   433	### How to spot it
   434	
   435	- `private lemma` in a file about well-established algebra/analysis
   436	  (Cauchy–Schwarz, `sqrt`, `rpow`, `PosSemidef`, `Matrix.trace`, etc.).
   437	- Custom structures named `MyX` / `LocalX` / `ProjectX` where `X` is a
   438	  standard concept.
   439	- Proof bodies that chain ten `private lemma`s where the natural Mathlib
   440	  counterpart would be two `exact?` lookups.
   441	- Files with no `import Mathlib.*` above the level of `Mathlib.Tactic.*`
   442	  when the subject matter is clearly Mathlib-adjacent (linear algebra,
   443	  analysis, measure theory).
   444

   371	   reference for the full Mathlib review guide.

- [ ] F1 (blocker) `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1946` — The `\leanok` support lemma quantifies over POVM polynomial measurements, but all three linked Lean conversions require `ProjMeas`.

## Review

F1 is a genuine statement-scope mismatch. `def:ld-meas` at `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:128-132` explicitly defines these measurements as POVMs, matching `lem:ld-soundness` in `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:413-438`, which produces measurements \(G^{\mathrm A},G^{\mathrm B}\). The linked Lean declarations instead require `ProjMeas` at `Defect.lean:110`, `:196`, and `:286-287`. Projectivity is not a Lean boundary condition; it restricts the mathematical domain and prevents applying these declarations directly to the POVMs supplied by the cited QPBT theorem.

Either generalize the conversion to complete POVMs, or explicitly state the projective restriction in the blueprint and stop presenting the node as an unrestricted consequence of QPBT `lem:ld-soundness`. The latter could instead cite the projective measurements produced by `thm:main-formal` at `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex:180-202`, especially line 188. The current `\leanok` must not remain on the broader statement.

F2 was not resolved by renaming the earlier `mature...` declaration. Its proof is exactly an application of `strategyConsRel_consistencyDefect_le`, and its only substantive consumer is the immediately following direct-coordinate theorem; the reverse direction already invokes the generic result directly. Inline that application and update the stacked branch rather than retaining a duplicate public specialization and compatibility alias.

The other prior findings are addressed: the Mathlib-duplicate sum lemma is gone, generic consistency and measurement lemmas are correctly placed, imports are direct, normalization is shared, and the blueprint now records the restricted coordinate and compression results. The facade type-check and `git diff --check` both pass. The authoritative patch introduces no `sorry`, axiom, or kernel bypass; its sole `sorry` match is the removed `ldGame.μ_prob` proof hole. Existing imported proof holes remain explicitly documented as named obligations.
